description: `is a <type-word>` with a word that is not a recognized Core type raises `ol-unknown-type` naming the word (spec/execution-model.md:146-166, error-model.md `ol-unknown-type`). Raised at stage=semantic: since issue #815 `execute()` runs the checker before Phase 2, so its copy is the one delivered. The runtime keeps an identical copy at stage=runtime for a caller driving `evaluate()`/`createEnvironment()` directly. The program does not run, so no event is emitted at all; under the `runUnchecked` opt-out execution halts at the failing statement and only its `instruction` event is kept. Issue #99. Issue #815: `execute()` now runs Layer 1 and Layer 2 before Phase 2 and refuses a program carrying an `error`-severity finding (`spec/execution-model.md:659-664`), so no event is emitted and the diagnostic delivered here is the CHECK's. The runtime's own copy of the rule still exists, but it runs only under the `runUnchecked` opt-out — NOT in this fixture, which is checked — and when it does run it is collapsed into the check's by the de-duplication rule (`spec/execution-model.md:741-748`), which is why the runtime's copy never appears beside the check's. So nothing here observes that copy, and reading this fixture as evidence for it would be a mistake: measured, a runtime guard can be deleted outright with the whole conformance corpus still green, because the surviving report is the check's either way. What the runtime copy uniquely contributes is that the run STOPS at the fault, which is written in the event stream rather than in the diagnostics and is pinned by `packages/runtime/src/runtime-guards-halt.test.mjs`.
